verdict.rationale: The first-party docs list official libraries for Rust (native) and TypeScript (web), FFI bindings for C, Python, Kotlin, Swift, Go and Dart, plus named packages such as @moq/watch, @moq/net, moq-net and Swift async sequences. A community report of building on and contributing to the Rust implementation corroborates real use. Missing for 10: depth and maturity of the FFI bindings (C, Python, Kotlin, Go, Dart) beyond a one-line mention, and independent hands-on evidence for SDKs other than Rust.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can build against official SDKs

citations.quote: Libraries for Rust (native) and TypeScript (web), plus FFI bindings for C, Python, Kotlin, Swift, Go, and Dart.
[@moq/watch](/lib/js/watch.html) - Subscribe to and render MoQ broadcasts, with an optional `<moq-watch>` UI.
[Swift](/lib/swift/) - Async sequences for iOS, iPadOS, and macOS.
Chat, game state, telemetry, and control channels over the same relays with [`moq-net`](/lib/rs/moq-net.html) or [`@moq/net`](/lib/js/net.html).
His fix PR was merged by Luke Curley.
